case.case: Case 18: Traffic control around a work area near an intersection, one lane closed
case.narrative: This scenario follows CDOT Standard Plan S-630-1, Case 18 (Sheet 10), "traffic control around a work area near an intersection, one lane closed", applied to a one-way street with every mainline warning and regulatory sign posted on both sides of the roadway per CDOT S-630-1 Sheet 2 General Note 8, plus a cross-street advance-warning set on each approach leg per MUTCD §6N.12 and the Sheet 10 advance-signing key.
case.narrative_2: Three disclosed departures from the plate: (1) the Case 18 plate typifies corner-quadrant work with a full cross-street closure train; this plan confines the work space to the mainline and places cross-street advance signing only. Corner-quadrant support is tracked at https://github.com/rtmakatura/conestruct/issues/128. (2) A one-way street has no opposing mainline direction; the plate's opposing-direction signing does not apply. (3) The plate typifies rural sign placement; urban applications require block-based placement per Sheet 10 Note 1. The plate's Type III corner barricade (work lasting more than 3 days) encloses the corner work area and is not placed, per departure (1).

flagger.source: MUTCD 11th Ed. Chapter 6D (Flagger Control) and Chapter 6E (One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control).

approaches.narrative: Each cross-street leg receives its own advance set (W20-1, R2-10, R2-11), computed from that leg's own speed and road type; stations are measured along the leg from the intersection curb line, increasing away from the intersection.
approaches.source: MUTCD §6N.12; CDOT S-630-1 Sheet 10, Cases 18/19 (advance-signing key)

turn_bay.text: Left-turn bay storage 150 ft, entered by operator (MUTCD TA-23 Note 5, p. 904: sized to hold the vehicles that turn left in one signal cycle). Lane-line channelizers run it from station 762 to the stop line at the upstream curb (612). The taper ends 100 ft before the bay (TA-23 draws 100 ft), with LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT (R3-7L) on the channelized island and on the far curb at station 862.
turn_bay.source: MUTCD 11th Ed. TA-23 (Fig. 6P-23, p. 905; Notes 4 and 5, p. 904)

pending_verification.note: On a one-way street the plan builds an 8 ft shoulder and fits lanes under a 52 ft half-road less that shoulder. Both values are CHOSEN: no MUTCD, S-630-1, Colorado Supplement or Denver text found sets them. Verify against the site (#308).

items.label: On a one-way street the plan builds an 8 ft shoulder and fits lanes under a 52 ft half-road less that shoulder. Both values are CHOSEN: no MUTCD, S-630-1, Colorado Supplement or Denver text found sets them. Verify against the site (#308).

The left lane's far side follows MUTCD 11th Ed. TA-23 (Fig. 6P-23, p. 905): the taper closes the left lane before the intersection and the lane reopens as a left-turn bay (Note 4, p. 904), with LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT on the channelized island and the far curb (Note 5). The bay's storage length was entered by the operator; this tool doesn't check it against the signal timing. Chosen where TA-23 leaves it open: the bay ends at the upstream curb line, standing in for the stop line; the 100 ft opening grows when the buffer reaches further; no centerline channelizers on a one-way street; the arrow board at the work space, as drawn; the closed lane stays channelized from the far curb to the work zone; the downstream end as on the right far side. Verify against the site (#323).

An adjacent intersection is flagged, but Conestruct does not generate the cross-street approach layout or evaluate traffic-signal operation, and adds no devices for it. Cross-street control design and the signal-operation review (MUTCD §6N.12, 11th Ed. p. 848; Part 4 for signal-head visibility) remain with the traffic control supervisor. Intersection support is tracked at issue #117; corner-quadrant work at issue #128.

Signalized approaches (cross_a, cross_b): Conestruct places cross-street advance signing only and does not evaluate traffic-signal operation. The signal-operation review remains with the traffic control supervisor and the operating agency: phasing, timing, and signal-head visibility per MUTCD §6N.12 (items 04 and 05; 11th Ed. p. 848) and MUTCD Part 4.

notes.rule: Denver is entity-gated: Contractor Licensing issues licenses to work in the ROW (720-865-2770), and the Street Occupancy Request Form requires a Contractor's license number.

Fee-design interaction (Rule 22.3 §IV.4.f, §IV.6.b): (1) maintain a temporary PAR or bike facility in the adjacent parking/travel lane -> that lane's closure fee is WAIVED; (2) fail to maintain 5 ft unobstructed width -> charged the FULL LENGTH OF A BLOCK for the sidewalk/bike closure; (3) covered walkway used as a detour with no added crossings -> reduced closure fee. The engine computes exactly the widths that decide this.
Bus stops: temporary relocation/closure requires written approval from BOTH the City Traffic Engineer and RTD; all accommodation costs on the Permittee.

Paid-parking closure -> separate parking meter permit obtained with the RSOP; meter head removal only by Transportation Operations, billed daily. Unauthorized permanent meter removal: fee = (total yearly meter revenue + citation revenue) x 15 — the largest penalty multiplier in the corpus (not renderable as a fixed meter).

Sheet requirements are the deepest in the corpus: the TCP must depict existing conditions (north arrow, speed limit, geometry, markings, lane assignments, curb lines, sidewalks, PAR, all light/utility/signal poles, all posted signage, bus stops, all parking meters and kiosks with counts, tree lawns, racks, drop boxes) plus proposed items and closure math (taper lengths, advance signage with type/placement/distances, arrow board, work zone length AND width, width of reduced travel lanes). Engine values + a site-survey layer.
Conflicting permits: first-submitted, first-served; coordination with existing permits required.
